samples.summary: `saveSnapshot()` moved inside `doc.batch()` suppresses the pre-edit cursor/selection flush, so undo after Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ restores a stale caret and selection
samples.evidence: `handleTab` (2703-2706), `handleIndent` (2763-2765) and `handleOutdent` (2780-2782) now call `this.saveSnapshot()` *inside* `this.doc.batch(...)`. In the full docs editor that callback is `editor.ts:2539-2552`, which calls `docStore.snapshot()` **and** `setCursorForHistory(cursor.position, selection.range)`. `YorkieDocStore.setCursorForHistory` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3048) delegates to `updateCursorPos`, whose presence write is deliberately skipped while a batch is open: `if (this.skipNonHistoryPresence()) return;` (3179) with `skipNonHistoryPresence() => this.activeRoot !== null` (3204). Its own docstring (3041-3046) states the flush must happen *before* the mutation because "Yorkie captures the *current* presence as the reverse of the mutation's `addToHistory` set, so the pre-edit selection must already be in presence when the mutation runs." `setBlockType` then records the reverse presence inside the batch (1534-1538). Because the live cursor publish is throttled (docs-view.tsx:452-469, `CURSOR_UPDATE_THROTTLE` with a trailing timer), the presence Yorkie reverses to can be the caret/selection from before the user's last move — the exact #609/#523 class of bug. The precedents the new comments cite (`withNamedStyleChange` at editor.ts:1239, `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` at link-run.ts:101) pass only `docStore.snapshot()`, which is a Yorkie no-op, so they are not evidence that the cursor-recording snapshot is safe inside a batch. Not observable in the docs vitest suite, which only exercises `MemDocStore`.

samples.summary: `siblingsOf` resolves the parent table with throwing `getBlock`, the opposite of the twin helper in editor.ts which uses `findBlock` for exactly this reason
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:2893 `const tableBlock = this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId);` — `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` (document.ts:215). `info` comes from `getCellInfo` → the layout's `blockParentMap`, which is only as fresh as the last layout pass, so a table removed by a remote edit since then leaves a stale entry. editor.ts:1636-1645 documents this hazard and deliberately uses `doc.findBlock` plus a `?? [block]` fallback "so a table removed since then would throw out of the middle of an indent gesture rather than degrade". The two twins disagree; the throw escapes `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` from inside `doc.batch()`, which rethrows after `refresh()` (document.ts:146-153) and aborts the whole Yorkie update.

samples.summary: markDirty for a carried child inside a NESTED table marks the inner table id, which is not a top-level layout block, so the child repaints at its old indent
samples.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` does `const cellInfo = doc.blockParentMap.get(change.block.id); markDirty(cellInfo?.tableBlockId ?? change.block.id);` — a single hop. For a list item in a cell of a table that is itself inside another table's cell, `tableBlockId` is the *inner* table, which never appears in `layout.blocks`, so `computeLayout`'s dirty check never invalidates the outer table's cached lines (layout.ts:456-515 reuses cached lines for a non-dirty table block). `indent()`/`outdent()` only call `render()` and never `invalidateLayout()`, so the carried child keeps its old x — the very failure the new markDirty was added to prevent. The repo already has a chain-walking helper for this shape (text-editor.ts:3768 `findOuterCellAddress`).

samples.summary: `siblingsOf`'s `?? [block]` fallback silently degrades the gesture to a single-block level change, which can produce the parent-at-child-level state the change exists to remove
samples.evidence: editor.ts:1642-1644: when `cellInfo` is stale (row/col index no longer exists after a remote row/column delete) `cell` is `undefined` and the helper returns `[block]`. `planSiblingGroup` then sees a one-element sibling array, finds no children, and moves only the caret's own item — reintroducing issue #1050's symptom instead of no-op'ing or degrading loudly. The comment only justifies avoiding a throw; it does not consider that the fallback bypasses the subtree invariant.

samples.summary: Outdenting a multi-item selection whose first item is at level 0 is now a total no-op, where the previous code still moved the deeper items up
samples.evidence: `planSiblingGroup` marks the whole subtree `covered` (line 90) *before* the boundary checks (93-94), so a refused root suppresses every selected descendant. Old code (e.g. text-editor.ts handleTab pre-change: `Math.max(0, currentLevel - 1)` per block) outdented the deeper members and left only the level-0 ones. Select an entire bulleted list and press Shift+Tab and nothing at all happens now. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md:25-33) records this as an intentional decision, hence the low confidence that it is unwanted — flagged because it is a user-visible behavior regression on a normal path.

samples.summary: One gesture now issues a write (plus a full document re-read) per block in the whole subtree, so Tab on the first item of a long list is O(N × document size)
samples.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` loops `doc.setBlockType(...)` over every block in the carried subtree; `Doc.setBlockType` calls `refresh()` (document.ts:662-667), and `MemDocStore.getDocument()` deep-clones the entire document via `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(doc))` (memory.ts:43-45). Previously only the *selected* blocks were written, so a single caret could cost one write; now a caret on a level-0 root of a 1000-item nested list costs ~1000 writes and ~2000 whole-document clones inside one synchronous batch (a UI freeze). The Yorkie path is cheaper per write but still N `styleByPath` writes in one change.

finding.summary: `siblingsOf` resolves the caret's container from the layout-time parent map; when that map has no entry for a cell block (created since the last layout) the returned sibling array does not contain the block, and the whole indent/outdent gesture becomes a silent no-op
finding.evidence: `siblingsOf` returns `doc.getContextBlocks()` when `doc.blockParentMap.get(block.id)` is undefined (editor.ts:1640; the same shape in text-editor.ts:2892 via `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`). The map is only rebuilt in `recomputeLayout`, and `Doc.findBlockInCells` documents exactly this staleness ("a block created since the last layout — e.g. the tail block a paste splits out inside a cell — isn't in it yet", document.ts:259-262) which is why it keeps a full-walk fallback. `siblingsOf` has no such fallback. For a cell-internal caret missing from the map, siblings resolve to the region's top-level blocks; `planSiblingGroup` then never finds the selected id in `blocks` and emits zero changes, so indent/outdent does nothing at all. Before this change `fn(block)` applied the level unconditionally, so the gesture always worked.
